## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to translate requirements into concrete ops: per-tenant resource isolation, knowledge of cgroup v2, and integration with systemd for session scope, plus a practical test and rollback plan.

## Key Concepts
- Cgroup v2 hierarchy and cpu.max
- Per-tenant slices (system.slice/tenant-<name>.slice)
- Attaching sessions to slices (systemd.slice) and fair scheduling
- Baseline latency measurement and a burst test
- Rollback safety and rollback steps

## Code Example
```
# Create per-tenant slices
sudo mkdir -p /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-a.slice
sudo mkdir -p /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-b.slice

# Limit each to 50% of a single CPU
echo "50000 100000" | sudo tee /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-a.slice/cpu.max
echo "50000 100000" | sudo tee /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-b.slice/cpu.max

# Example: bind a login session to a tenant slice (conceptual)
sudo systemd-run --slice=tenant-a.slice -t --unit=ssh-session tenant-a-login
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you automate tenant-to-slice assignment for new users?
- What monitoring would you add to detect drift or fairness violations, and how would you alert on them?

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question assesses practical, beginner-friendly problem-solving skills for real-world I/O contention in multi-tenant Linux environments. It evaluates the ability to implement measurable fixes, maintain safe rollback procedures, and use standard tooling instead of ad-hoc solutions.

## Key Concepts

- **fio**: A flexible I/O testing tool used to establish baseline metrics and validate performance improvements after configuration changes

## Why This Question Is Asked

- **BPF observability**: Enables per-cgroup telemetry without significant overhead, allowing real-time visibility into I/O patterns and latency distribution.

## Why This Is Asked

- User/group membership and least-privilege access

- Safe testing of privileges without exposing broad rights

## Code Example
```bash
id user; groups user
sudo -l -U user
cp /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.bak
printf 'user ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:/usr/bin/systemctl restart myservice\n' > /etc/sudoers.d/user
visudo -cf /etc/sudoers.d/user
sudo -n /usr/bin/systemctl restart myservice
```
